rowdata.pxWarningMessage: Writing application logic using the Java activity method impacts maintainability, discourages reusability, and increases risk during upgrades. Use this method only when necessary. If executing Java code is required, consider using the Call-Function activity method to execute a Function rule. Using Function rules encourages creating well-defined input and output parameters and can be reused across many different types of rules.
This activity has more than 25 steps. Consider decomposing this activity into smaller, more modular pieces.

When acquiring a lock using Obj-Open or Obj-Refresh-And-Lock you should always check to make sure the lock was actually granted. This is commonly done using StepStatusFail in the transition of the step acquiring the lock or in the precondition of the step immediately after the lock is acquired.
Max Records has not been specified on the Obj-Browse method. If left blank, the value will default to 10,000. Consider specifying a maximum limit for improved query performance.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
The call to activity 'DeleteAttachment' contains the AppliesTo class name 'Work-'. Consider defining a step page of that AppliesTo class in the activity call instead.
Be careful not to write sensitive or confidential information, including encrypted properties and any properties from encrypted BLOBs, to logs.
You should create a test case for this rule to identify any regression issues that might occur when this rule is modified.
